001_baseline.title: Baseline Matching & Filtering Comparisons
key_findings: Spatial-only indexing retrieves proximate candidates but suffers high false-positive rates.
Zero-tolerance feasibility filtering eliminates invalid directions and departure mismatches.

002_ablation.title: Leave-One-Rule-Out Feasibility Ablation
key_findings: Directional bearing alignment is the single most critical filter preventing opposite-direction pairings.
Detour thresholding prevents unacceptably circuitous passenger pickups.

003_robustness.title: Correlated Spatial and Temporal Noise Robustness
key_findings: Spatial noise <= 100m causes negligible ranking degradation (< 1.5% NDCG shift).
Vehicle availability dropouts represent the dominant point of operational failure.

004_heldout.title: Cross-Corridor Held-Out Generalization
004_heldout.benchmark_scope: Thin vs balanced vs dense corridor distributions
key_findings: Heuristic ranking generalizes stably across densities without parameter overfitting.
Thin demand density limits precision due to a structural deficit of complementary pairs.

005_classical_ml.title: Supervised Ranking via Classical Machine Learning
005_classical_ml.benchmark_scope: Feature engineering and logistic regression ranking
key_findings: Supervised logistic regression achieves high ranking fidelity (0.797 NDCG@3).
However, rule heuristics slightly edge out ML (0.824 NDCG@3) on clean synthetic features without training overhead.

006_road_network.title: Empirical Street-Level Circuity Factor Benchmark
key_findings: Street network distance is on average 34.1% longer than Euclidean distance.
One-way street restrictions force peak circuity up to 3.075x straight-line distance.

007_assignment_scaling.title: Multi-Rider Batch Assignment Optimality & Scaling
key_findings: Greedy assignment executes in < 1 ms while maintaining a 10–17% optimality gap relative to exact branch-and-bound.
Exact branch-and-bound search complexity explodes exponentially on cohorts >= 30x15.

008_road_network_validation.title: Realistic Road-Network Matching Validation
008_road_network_validation.benchmark_scope: Downtown SF network (26 nodes, 53 edges, 45 candidate pairs)
key_findings: 75.6% (34/45) of geometric candidate pairs are road-network false positives that fail true turn-constrained routing.
Evaluating true road routing increases Precision@1 from 0.120 to 0.400.
Road network routing is ~21.5x more computationally expensive than Euclidean evaluation.

009_hybrid_pruning.title: Hybrid Two-Tier Candidate Pruning & Admissible Bounds
009_hybrid_pruning.benchmark_scope: Two-tier geometric bounding before Dijkstra search
key_findings: Admissible lower-bound pruning eliminates 81.8% of expensive road-network evaluations with 0 false negatives.
Guarantees 100% feasible recall and 100% top-1 recommendation agreement while achieving a 5.49x speedup.
Aggressive heuristic circuity pruning induces a catastrophic 85.7% false negative rate.

010_dynamic_congestion.title: Dynamic Congestion Curves & Peak-Hour Robustness
010_dynamic_congestion.evidence_class: OSM road network with BPR congestion curves
010_dynamic_congestion.benchmark_scope: Free-flow vs mild vs moderate vs severe congestion across departure offsets
key_findings: Severe congestion inflates travel times by 3.8x and slashes feasible candidate pairs by 70.6% (17 down to 5).
Top-1 recommendations shift by 16.7% between free-flow and peak hours, proving static routing is obsolete.

011_multi_rider_pooling.title: Multi-Rider Capacity Pooling under Dynamic Congestion
011_multi_rider_pooling.evidence_class: Capacity-pooled tour optimization on road network
011_multi_rider_pooling.benchmark_scope: Vehicle capacities C=1..4 under dynamic BPR traffic
key_findings: Expanding vehicle capacity from C=1 to C=2 boosts rider matching from 40.0% to 68.0% (+70% relative gain).
Peak congestion shifts the optimal waypoint visiting sequence in 20.0% of pooled tours.
Proven exact optimality gap averages 26.94% on small tractable instances.

012_dynamic_recourse.title: Dynamic Curbside Dwell, Incidents & Online Recourse
012_dynamic_recourse.evidence_class: Dynamic road network with incidents and stochastic dwell
012_dynamic_recourse.benchmark_scope: 6 operating conditions across mild/moderate/severe disruptions and 3 seeds
key_findings: Arterial link closures reduce static plan feasibility to 50–60% due to impassable closures.
Online recourse completely restores feasibility to 100.0% with sub-4ms computational latency.
Online recourse reduces oracle regret from 35.86 points down to 5.42 points.

013_rolling_dispatch.title: Fleet-Wide Rolling-Horizon Dispatch Simulation
013_rolling_dispatch.evidence_class: Discrete-event fleet simulation on OSM road graph
013_rolling_dispatch.benchmark_scope: Low, Balanced, and High demand regimes across 3 dispatch policies
key_findings: Event-driven rolling dispatch with active-trip insertions cuts fleet mileage by 60.5% in balanced demand and 72.0% in high demand.
Eliminating batch quantization windows cuts median passenger waiting time by 39.1% (103s vs 169s).
Incremental event-driven matching executes in 0.99 ms on average (p95 = 4.18 ms), providing real-time production viability.

H1_multi_objective_pooling.research_question: RQ1: How do matching objectives affect pooling and rider cost?
H1_multi_objective_pooling.formal_statement: Under identical constraints, multi-objective pooling produces higher pooling rates than a no-pooling baseline, at a measurable detour cost.
H1_multi_objective_pooling.empirical_evidence: Expanding vehicle capacity C=1 to C=2 increased rider fulfillment from 40.0% to 68.0% (Exp 011). In Exp 013, dynamic pooling raised sharing from 0.0% to 100.0%, cutting fleet VKT by 60.5% (50.5 km vs 127.8 km) with a mean detour cost of 2.93 km.
H1_multi_objective_pooling.caveats_and_limitations: Detour penalties must be tightly bounded (<= 3.5 km); otherwise rider duration inflates by > 49%, reducing utility.

H2_uncertainty_and_congestion.research_question: RQ2: How sensitive is matching to time and route uncertainty?
H2_uncertainty_and_congestion.formal_statement: Increasing uncertainty bounds reduces feasible matches unless the matcher explicitly models uncertainty.
H2_uncertainty_and_congestion.empirical_evidence: Severe congestion reduced feasible candidates by 70.6% and inverted 16.7% of top-1 matches (Exp 010). Arterial closures caused 40-50% feasibility failure in static plans, whereas dynamic recourse restored feasibility to 100% (Exp 012).
H2_uncertainty_and_congestion.caveats_and_limitations: Small spatial perturbations (<= 100m) cause negligible disruption (< 1.5% NDCG); disruptions become catastrophic primarily at structural network bottlenecks (closures/severe choke points).

H3_compute_quality_frontier.research_question: RQ3: What is the compute/quality frontier between exact optimization and heuristics?
H3_compute_quality_frontier.formal_statement: Heuristics reduce latency relative to exact optimization on larger instances, with a quality loss that must be reported rather than assumed.
H3_compute_quality_frontier.empirical_evidence: Exact branch-and-bound scaled exponentially (timeout at 5x8 in Exp 011 and > 1.1s at 20x10 in Exp 007). Greedy heuristics execute in < 1 ms with a proven 10-17% optimality gap on small instances (Exp 007) and 26.9% on multi-rider pooling (Exp 011). Two-tier pruning achieves 5.49x speedup with 0 false negatives (Exp 009).
H3_compute_quality_frontier.caveats_and_limitations: Heuristics do not establish global theoretical upper bounds; optimality gaps widen as vehicle capacity and candidate density scale.

RQ4_fairness_and_equity.research_question: RQ4: Are benefits and burdens distributed equitably?
RQ4_fairness_and_equity.formal_statement: Examine detour and wait time disparity across spatial corridors.
RQ4_fairness_and_equity.empirical_evidence: In Exp 006 and 008, one-way street geometry created severe asymmetric circuity (up to 3.075x on northern arterials vs 1.1x on parallel streets). In Exp 013, p95 waiting times reached 251s while median wait was 103s.
RQ4_fairness_and_equity.caveats_and_limitations: Synthetic datasets lack demographic or socioeconomic labels by design; spatial burden disparities are driven by network topology rather than explicit equity objectives.

RQ5_explanations_and_acceptance.research_question: RQ5: Do explanations improve appropriate acceptance?
RQ5_explanations_and_acceptance.formal_statement: Explanations and feature contribution transparency enhance system predictability.
RQ5_explanations_and_acceptance.empirical_evidence: Rule-based interpretable linear weights (0-100) allow exact attribution of compatibility penalties (bearing, detour, pickup proximity). Logistic regression weights corroborated human-intuitive feature importance in Exp 005.
RQ5_explanations_and_acceptance.caveats_and_limitations: Requires real-world human-in-the-loop user studies to confirm user cognitive trust and behavioral acceptance.

ranking_quality_vs_heuristics.tension: Complex supervised models vs transparent rule-based linear indices.
ranking_quality_vs_heuristics.low_cost_regime: Rule-based weighted index (Exp 001, 004): 0.824 NDCG@3, zero training, instant auditability.
ranking_quality_vs_heuristics.high_fidelity_regime: Supervised logistic regression (Exp 005): 0.797 NDCG@3, learns feature weights, requires labeled training data.
ranking_quality_vs_heuristics.measured_impact: On clean synthetic features, transparent rule heuristics match or slightly outperform ML (+0.027 NDCG), avoiding distribution shift.
ranking_quality_vs_heuristics.recommended_operating_point: Deploy transparent rule-based scoring for candidate retrieval, reserving ML for user-acceptance personalization.

road_network_accuracy_vs_euclidean.tension: Rapid straight-line geometric approximation vs turn-constrained street graph topology.
road_network_accuracy_vs_euclidean.low_cost_regime: Euclidean distance: ~45 us/pair, 0 graph memory, ignores one-way restrictions and turn constraints.
road_network_accuracy_vs_euclidean.high_fidelity_regime: Network-aware Dijkstra: ~974 us/pair (21.5x slower), respects one-way streets, turn delays, and network topology.
road_network_accuracy_vs_euclidean.measured_impact: Euclidean gating incurs a 75.6% false-positive rate (34/45 pairs invalid in Exp 008) and 68% top-1 rank disagreement.
road_network_accuracy_vs_euclidean.recommended_operating_point: Never use raw Euclidean distance for final dispatch; always evaluate true street graph shortest paths.

routing_latency_vs_expansion.dimension_name: Routing Latency vs Exact Graph Search
routing_latency_vs_expansion.tension: Sub-millisecond query requirements vs multi-stop Dijkstra path search overhead.
routing_latency_vs_expansion.low_cost_regime: Straight-line / approximate geometry: ~45 us/call, enables 20,000 evaluations/second.
routing_latency_vs_expansion.high_fidelity_regime: Full Dijkstra routing on multi-stop pooled routes: 4-15 ms per vehicle permutation (Exp 011).
routing_latency_vs_expansion.measured_impact: Unconstrained multi-stop road routing induces combinatorial explosion (O(n! 2^n) stops), violating interactive SLA.
routing_latency_vs_expansion.recommended_operating_point: Enforce early-stopping branch pruning and precomputed contraction-hierarchy distance tables for road networks.

pruning_recall_vs_search_speedup.tension: Aggressive heuristic candidate filtering vs provably admissible bounding.
pruning_recall_vs_search_speedup.low_cost_regime: Heuristic circuity pruning (Exp 009): 97.8% pruned, but 85.7% false negatives (discards valid matches).
pruning_recall_vs_search_speedup.high_fidelity_regime: Admissible lower-bound pruning (Exp 009): 81.8% pruned, 5.49x speedup, exactly 0 false negatives, 100% recall.
pruning_recall_vs_search_speedup.measured_impact: Admissible bounds eliminate over 80% of Dijkstra calls without sacrificing a single feasible pair.
pruning_recall_vs_search_speedup.recommended_operating_point: Deploy two-tier admissible Euclidean lower-bound pruning as a mandatory pre-filter before road routing.

assignment_optimality_vs_solver_runtime.tension: Global branch-and-bound optimization vs greedy priority queue heuristics.
assignment_optimality_vs_solver_runtime.low_cost_regime: Greedy insertion: < 1 ms runtime across all tested scales, provable 10-17% optimality gap.
assignment_optimality_vs_solver_runtime.high_fidelity_regime: Exact branch-and-bound: guarantees 0% gap, but times out or exceeds 1.1s on cohorts >= 20x10.
assignment_optimality_vs_solver_runtime.measured_impact: In dynamic real-time operations, solver latency must remain < 5 ms; exact solvers cannot scale to fleet sizes.
assignment_optimality_vs_solver_runtime.recommended_operating_point: Use greedy insertion for real-time online dispatch, utilizing exact solvers only for offline benchmark auditing.

pooling_capacity_vs_detour_burden.dimension_name: Vehicle Pooling Capacity vs Passenger Detour Burden
pooling_capacity_vs_detour_burden.tension: High vehicle passenger capacity vs individual rider travel-time inflation.
pooling_capacity_vs_detour_burden.low_cost_regime: Single-occupancy C=1 (Exp 011): 0 rider detour, but only 40.0% matching fulfillment.
pooling_capacity_vs_detour_burden.high_fidelity_regime: Multi-rider pooling C=2..4 (Exp 011): 68-72% matching fulfillment (+70%), but 1.22x rider duration and 2.0x detour.
pooling_capacity_vs_detour_burden.measured_impact: Capacity C=2 captures the vast majority of pooling benefits (68% matched) while keeping detour reasonable (5.5 min). Higher capacities yield diminishing returns.
pooling_capacity_vs_detour_burden.recommended_operating_point: Standardize on vehicle capacity C=2 for private-car pooling, enforcing a 3.5 km hard detour cap.

congestion_delay_vs_recourse_adaptation.dimension_name: Congestion Delay & Recourse vs Static Plan Fragility
congestion_delay_vs_recourse_adaptation.tension: Pre-planned static dispatch vs dynamic reactive route adaptation.
congestion_delay_vs_recourse_adaptation.low_cost_regime: Static unadapted execution (Exp 012): 0 online compute overhead, but 40-50% feasibility failure under closures.
congestion_delay_vs_recourse_adaptation.high_fidelity_regime: Online recourse (Exp 012): 3.42 ms latency, evaluates alternate sequences, restores feasibility to 100%.
congestion_delay_vs_recourse_adaptation.measured_impact: Online recourse recovers 76.7% of lost objective score and cuts oracle regret from 35.86 to 5.42 points.
congestion_delay_vs_recourse_adaptation.recommended_operating_point: Equip all active pooled vehicles with online incident recourse routers operating with sub-5ms local replanning.

rolling_dispatch_vs_batch_quantization.dimension_name: Rolling-Horizon Dispatch vs Batch Quantization Delay
rolling_dispatch_vs_batch_quantization.tension: Fixed-interval batching (60s) vs continuous event-driven replanning.
rolling_dispatch_vs_batch_quantization.low_cost_regime: Static batching (Exp 013): fixed 60s windows, no active-trip insertions, Fleet VKT = 127.8 km, p50 wait = 169s.
rolling_dispatch_vs_batch_quantization.high_fidelity_regime: Event-driven rolling dispatch (Exp 013): immediate trigger on arrivals/stops/cancellations, Fleet VKT = 50.5 km (-60.5%), p50 wait = 103s (-39.1%).
rolling_dispatch_vs_batch_quantization.measured_impact: Active-trip insertion and zero quantization delay break supply bottlenecks, dramatically reducing fleet mileage and wait times.
rolling_dispatch_vs_batch_quantization.recommended_operating_point: Standardize platform dispatch on event-driven rolling horizon with active-trip waypoint insertions.

construct_validity: Detour is modeled as Euclidean or directed shortest-path distance, which does not account for real-time curbside parking search time or passenger walking access.
Compatibility score weights (0-100) are empirically chosen heuristics rather than derived from revealed-preference passenger econometric models.
internal_validity: BPR congestion curves approximate macro-scale traffic flow rather than microscopic car-following behavior (SUMO/Aimsun).
Turn penalties and traffic signal delays are modeled via fixed junction time additions rather than dynamic cycle phasing.
Patience thresholds are sampled from stationary log-normal distributions without modeling passenger surge-pricing willingness.
external_validity: Road-network validation is restricted to a bounded Downtown San Francisco corridor (26 nodes, 53 edges); suburban or multi-hub networks may exhibit different circuity distributions.
Synthetic commuter travel demands follow parameterized OD corridors rather than empirical census/LEHD origin-destination survey matrices.
Vehicle fleet sizes (8-20 drivers) are small compared to city-wide commercial fleets (thousands of vehicles).
reproducibility_and_leakage: All experiments use deterministic pseudo-random seeds (e.g. 42, 101, 2024) and LCG state generation.
Evaluated candidate pools strictly prevent train/test leakage across held-out seeds.
No wall-clock dependencies exist in algorithmic decisions; all simulations proceed via discrete event queues.

key_system_breakthroughs: Two-tier admissible pruning cuts road network routing calls by 81.8% with 0 false negatives.
Network-aware Dijkstra routing eliminates 75.6% false-positive match rate incurred by Euclidean gating.
Multi-rider pooling C=2 increases rider matching by +70% relative to single-occupancy fleets.
Online recourse completely restores 100% trip feasibility under arterial road closures in <= 4.3 ms.
Event-driven rolling dispatch with active-trip insertions slashes fleet VKT by 60.5% and median wait time by 39.1%.
